text:
Researchers at the Cooperative Fishery Research Unit, Montana State University, Bozeman, have conducted an aquatic resources study on Sarpy Creek for Westmoreland Resources (Dames and Moore, 1975). Fish species, aquatic invertebrates, bottom material composition, and stream side vegetation were studied in the lease area and downstream to the Yellowstone River.
Benthic Organisms - Stream bottom composition in Sarpy Creek is primarily classified as muck (See Table II-16). This condition is explained by the abundance of plant material in or near the streambed, and the normally very sluggish current found in the stream (Dames & Moore, 1975). Organic materials found in the substrate include fiberous peat and detritus; both are common in the streambed.
Twenty-six families of aquatic invertebrates were classified from bottom samples collected from Sarpy Creek. These families are listed in Appendix F. The upper sections of Sarpy Creek and East Fork of Sarpy Creek are dominated by species that prefer soft, muddy substrates and slow-moving waters.
